blockers.quote: What if your money doubled every day?
blockers.why: Checks #3 and #15 fail: the premise question arrives around 0:40, and by 0:30 the viewer still lacks the exact-zero danger and the question driving the film.
blockers.fix: Compress lines 22–50 so the midnight doubling lands by 0:12, then begin by 0:15 with: “What if your money doubled every day? Every night, whatever is there doubles. It will not stop. Can you reach zero before Lotte’s bread moves out of reach?”

blockers.quote: > SCENE: Day forty. The back door of the bakery. The flour man, arms folded, a sack half off the van. Lotte, the baker, in the doorway. Above the oven behind her, her grandfather's framed banknote from the bad year, a picture only.
blockers.why: The “No new person after 60%” check fails: the flour man first appears around 62% of the film.
blockers.fix: Plant the same flour man in line 249’s balloon scene, unloading sacks beside Lotte without speaking; line 282 then becomes his return.

blockers.quote: Mansa Musa once came through Cairo and gave away so much gold that gold there stayed cheap for at least twelve years (c06). Your street learns it by the weekend.
blockers.why: Check #13 fails: the fact follows an outcome already demonstrated and changes neither the next action nor anyone’s feeling.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “Mansa Musa’s gifts kept gold cheap in Cairo for at least twelve years (c06). Jonas looks from Lotte’s new price to your phone. You offer it. He steps back.”

suggestions.quote: Day twenty-eight. One point three million. You buy the building. The bakery, the flats, the lot. Lotte never pays rent again.
suggestions.fix: Strengthen the connector from the bank beat: “You told the bank it was yours. So you spend it where you owe the most. Day twenty-eight. You buy the building.”
Replace the familiar age misunderstanding with a premise-specific escalation: “Lotte: Thirty-one yesterday. Sixty-two now.” Then show a second delivery arriving because you doubled the order.

suggestions.quote: That's it. That's the moment. She says it to everyone.
suggestions.fix: Cut this line and let Lotte’s “I saw” and Jonas asking for a receipt carry the anticlimax without narration.

keep.quote: Jonas: I don't know what to do with my hands when they win.
It isn't taken from anyone. Except it is. From everyone. A little. Every night.
A coin isn't a thing. It's Lotte, agreeing to bake tomorrow.
